title: Substrings That Rearrange Into Palindromes
src: MathWorks OA, IIT Bombay, 2026 (Software Engineer role). Coding question 2 of 3.
body:
You are given several strings of lowercase letters. For each string, count its substrings (contiguous, non-empty, counted by position) whose letters can be rearranged to form a palindrome.

A multiset of letters can form a palindrome exactly when at most one letter occurs an odd number of times.
inp: The first line contains T. Each of the next T lines contains one string.
out: T lines: the count for each string. Counts can exceed 231.

samples.ex: aba: a, b, a, aba (ab and ba have two odd letters): 4. abc: only the three single letters: 3.
The 4 single letters, aa and bb, aab and abb (one odd letter each), and aabb itself: 4 + 2 + 2 + 1 = 9. ab has two odd letters, so it doesn't count.

import sys

def count(s):
    seen = {0: 1}; mask = 0; total = 0
    for ch in s:
        mask ^= 1 << (ord(ch) - 97)
        total += seen.get(mask, 0)               # every letter even
        for b in range(26):                       # exactly one letter odd
            total += seen.get(mask ^ (1 << b), 0)
        seen[mask] = seen.get(mask, 0) + 1
    return total

def main():
    t = sys.stdin.read().split()
    print("\n".join(str(count(s)) for s in t[1:1 + int(t[0])]))

main()
